newsitem.title: USA: U.S. banking stocks jump ahead of economic reports.
newsitem.headline: U.S. banking stocks jump ahead of economic reports.

text.p: Banking and financial stocks jumped on Monday as some traders bet that economic reports due this week would not indicate an overheating U.S. economy.

Shares of the biggest U.S. banks were showing solid gains near the close, with Chase Manhattan Corp shares rising 2-5/8 to 88, Citicorp climbing 4-1/2 to 107-7/8, BankAmerica Corp up 3-1/2 to 110-7/8 and NationsBank Corp adding 5/8 to 58-7/8. Shares of J.P. Morgan & Co Inc rose 2-3/4 to 98-5/8.
The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's bank index rose more than 14 points, or 2.5 percent, to nearly 568.

Traders and analysts cited several reasons for the strong move by banking issues, including gains in the bond market on, an overdue rebound by the sector, and strong earnings posted by banks during the last few weeks.

One trader at Shields & Co said some investors were betting that a slew of economic reports due this week would not point to accelerating inflation, which could mean the Federal Reserve may not raise interest rates anytime soon.
In late trading, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was up 11/32 to yield 7.11 percent.
Jim Benning, a trader at BT Brokerage, said the banking sector overall "got roughed up pretty well and is now getting a bit of a bounce back".
Compared with the Dow Jones industrial average, the Philadelphia stock exchange's banking index suffered sharper losses in the correction that toppled both the indexes from their March 10 peaks.
The banking index is currently up 5.5 percent this year, compared with 20.7 percent at its summit. The Dow is up five percent in 1997, compared with a gain of 9.8 percent at its peak.
